section_summary: This section traces U.S., British, and Netherlands discussions of petroleum exports to Japan, including export quotas, licensing, payment controls, and the risk that restrictions might prompt Japanese action against the Netherlands East Indies. It also contains a detailed U.S. Navy intelligence study of Japan’s oil imports, reserves, tankers, storage, and prospects for self-sufficiency. Later correspondence concerns particular shipments, Japanese requests for oil, and coordination of export policy.

subfiles.title: Comparative effects of petroleum export quota plans
subfiles.about: Compares two proposed quarterly U.S. petroleum export quotas for Japan.
subfiles.summary: Table compares quotas based on 1936 exports and the 1937–1940 average.

subfiles.title: Oil Plays Vital Part in Pacific Diplomacy Pertaining to War
subfiles.about: Reports how Japanese oil purchases from the Indies may reduce California exports to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Article links Pacific oil trade to diplomacy and forecasts reduced California sales to Japan.

subfiles.title: Far Eastern Affairs comments on petroleum exports to Japan
subfiles.about: Comments on proposals to restrict U.S. petroleum exports to Japan.
subfiles.summary: The division warns that sharp restrictions might induce Japan to seize Netherlands East Indies oil. It favors avoiding substantial cuts for now, while considering limits on tankers and metal containers.

subfiles.title: Request for comments on oil-company meeting background
subfiles.about: Requests comments before the Secretary meets an American oil-company president.
subfiles.summary: Requests suggestions on a background memorandum for the January 14 meeting.

subfiles.title: Background memorandum on petroleum exports to the Far East
subfiles.about: Reviews the political and military implications of petroleum sales to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Discusses the aviation gasoline restriction, Japanese purchases just below its octane threshold, and the East Indies oil agreement. It expresses concern about Japanese stockpiles and oil shipped in drums, while suggesting voluntary restraint by exporters and less provision of tankers and metal containers.

subfiles.title: Conversation with N. M. Butler about British oil memoranda
subfiles.about: Records Butler’s complaint that Britain had not received a reply on oil policy.
subfiles.summary: Butler supplied revised memoranda on Japan and Thailand and described British frustration over the lack of response. Hornbeck suggested placing them with the Secretary or Under Secretary.

subfiles.title: Japanese Embassy request concerning lubricating oil on Azuma Maru
subfiles.about: Seeks permission to move restricted lubricating oil to the Pacific Coast for export.
subfiles.summary: The Embassy says Mitsubishi Shoji Kaisha cannot resell the oil domestically and asks that it be allowed to export it.

subfiles.title: Reply to Japanese Embassy on lubricating oil shipment
subfiles.about: Explains that the proposed lubricating oil shipment requires an export license.
subfiles.summary: The Department offers to refer an application once filed.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference to Standard-Vacuum inquiry on export restrictions
subfiles.about: Points to a memorandum concerning Standard-Vacuum’s request for U.S. export-policy guidance.
subfiles.summary: References a July 10 letter delivered by A. G. May to Hamilton.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference to suspected oil-field equipment transshipment
subfiles.about: Points to a report suspecting oil-field equipment bought by William Smith was destined for Japan.
subfiles.summary: Records suspected transshipment and a shipment held at Laredo.

subfiles.title: Japan oil situation
subfiles.from: A. R. McCollum, Office of the Chief of Naval Operations
subfiles.to: Navy Department and Department of State
subfiles.about: Assesses Japan’s petroleum imports, reserves, tanker capacity, storage, production, and wartime endurance.
subfiles.summary: The report argues that Japan relies heavily on U.S. crude oil, aviation fuel components, and lubricants, and that licensing restrictions have not stopped useful fuel exports. It compiles import statistics, tanker capacity, storage locations, domestic and synthetic production, and consumption controls. It estimates roughly 75.5 million barrels in reserves at the end of 1940 and concludes that reserves plus domestic production could sustain substantial military use during an embargo or blockade.

subfiles.title: Routing comment on Japanese tankers seeking special crude
subfiles.about: Flags eight tankers scheduled to load high-octane San Joaquin Valley crude.
subfiles.summary: Notes the delayed routing of a Customs report and absence of recommendations.

subfiles.title: Customs report on future oil shipments to Japan
subfiles.about: Forwards a deputy collector’s report on planned oil shipments.
subfiles.summary: Offers to take special action if the State Department requests it.

subfiles.title: Scheduled Japanese tanker loadings at Estero Bay
subfiles.about: Lists eight Japanese tankers scheduled to load special San Joaquin Valley crude.
subfiles.summary: Reports expected arrivals, export licenses, and the crude’s usefulness for producing aviation motor fuel.

subfiles.title: Walden letter on Japanese gasoline request from Shanghai
subfiles.about: Reports a request for a tanker cargo of motor gasoline for Japanese forces in Shanghai.
subfiles.summary: Walden says Standard-Vacuum declined to quote and alerts State that Japan may seek other suppliers.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment of Walden’s August 25 letter
subfiles.about: Acknowledges Walden’s report of the Shanghai gasoline request.
subfiles.summary: Thanks Walden for the telegram and his reply.

subfiles.title: Comment on Japanese oil-import figures
subfiles.about: Comments on Walden’s evidence that Japanese imports exceeded consumption.
subfiles.summary: Observes that figures support the view that Japan built substantial required oil stocks.

subfiles.title: Walden letter forwarding Shell oil-import data
subfiles.about: Forwards Shell figures showing why 1935–1936 Japanese oil imports were abnormal.
subfiles.summary: Walden attributes the high imports to Japan’s six-month reserve requirement.

subfiles.title: Shell summary of Japanese petroleum imports and consumption
subfiles.about: Argues that 1935–1936 exports are an inflated basis for Netherlands Indies quotas.
subfiles.summary: Tabulates civilian consumption and imports, highlighting oil imported beyond apparent civilian needs.

subfiles.title: Shell note for Hoel Hall on Netherlands Indies export calculations
subfiles.about: Explains Shell’s objections to using 1935–1936 exports as a quota base.
subfiles.summary: Says Shell has sent supporting figures and relevant cables to interested representatives.

subfiles.title: Godber cable on abnormal 1935–1936 Japanese oil imports
subfiles.about: Supplies figures challenging proposed export quotas based on 1935–1936.
subfiles.summary: Compares civilian consumption, civilian imports, and government imports through 1940 and argues that civilian imports included government stockbuilding.

subfiles.title: Cable on Netherlands Indies petroleum export controls
subfiles.about: Relays unofficial information on Netherlands Indies export specifications and quantities.
subfiles.summary: Reports possible U.S.-aligned product rules, a ban on crude exports, and a quota based on 1935–1936.

subfiles.title: Godber follow-up on proposed quota base
subfiles.about: Clarifies that a percentage of 1935–1936 trade may set the Indies quota.
subfiles.summary: Promises figures showing those years were unusually high.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment of Walden’s August 28 letter
subfiles.about: Acknowledges the Shell data on Japanese petroleum imports from 1929 to 1940.
subfiles.summary: Thanks Walden and Shell for supplying the figures.

subfiles.title: Conversations on Standard-Vacuum’s blocked balances
subfiles.about: Records Walden’s inquiry about receiving Japanese payment and a consultation with Treasury.
subfiles.summary: Walden reported prospective payment of blocked yen balances and asked about an unfreezing license. State and Treasury saw no objection to payment in free dollars, but Treasury was unwilling to authorize payment from an already blocked account.

subfiles.title: Conversation with van Boetzelaer on petroleum quotas and payment rules
subfiles.about: Discusses coordination of U.S. and Netherlands Indies petroleum export and payment policies.
subfiles.summary: Van Boetzelaer describes concern that export licenses without payment licenses could mislead Japan and reports Indies refusals of tanker shipments. He outlines a proposed lower annual quota and says the Netherlands might stop all petroleum exports if the United States did likewise. The memorandum also examines Japanese blocked funds and imports needed by the Indies.

subfiles.title: Conversation with van Boetzelaer on payment for exports to Japan
subfiles.about: Clarifies how Japan could pay for licensed petroleum shipments under U.S. freezing rules.
subfiles.summary: Hiss confirms that frozen Japanese funds could not presently pay for petroleum exports and discusses possible use of free dollars. Van Boetzelaer reports Indies tanker refusals and seeks clarification on proceeds from Japanese imports, including silk.

subfiles.title: Conversation on Standard-Vacuum stocks in Shanghai
subfiles.about: Requests detailed estimates of Standard-Vacuum’s oil supply needs in China.
subfiles.summary: Lowden and Murch affirm that stocks in North China and Manchuria cover no more than about two months. They agree to separate those requirements from Shanghai retail and industrial needs.

subfiles.title: Cover memorandum on Japanese payment proposal and Taiwan bonds
subfiles.about: Forwards a Treasury conversation record and comments on delayed decisions.
subfiles.summary: Notes pending oil-payment review and an incomplete application concerning Taiwan Electric Power Company bonds.

subfiles.title: Nishiyama meeting on tanker payments and Taiwan bonds
subfiles.about: Records Nishiyama’s inquiries about oil-shipment payments and bond sinking-fund operations.
subfiles.summary: Treasury had not decided the payment proposal; Nishiyama said the delay kept Japanese tankers in West Coast ports.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference to Justice Department petroleum report
subfiles.about: Points to a memorandum on Japan’s petroleum situation and industrial activities.
subfiles.summary: References a Justice Department letter and enclosed petroleum memorandum.

subfiles.title: Paraphrase of report from Lima on fuel oil for Japanese ships
subfiles.about: Reports instructions to withhold most fuel oil deliveries to Japanese ships.
subfiles.summary: Says limited promised fuel will be delivered and mentions a report concerning the Ginyo Maru.
